yes-no.title: Yes / no
yes-no.description: A boolean choice. The question's inline response schema is a boolean; this element renders Yes / No controls. Optional custom button labels.

single-select.title: Single choice
single-select.description: Pick exactly one option (multiple-choice). The response schema is an enum of option ids; the options live in props.

multi-select.title: Select all that apply
multi-select.description: Pick any number of options (select-all). The response schema is an array of option ids; the options live in props. Optional min_selections / max_selections bound how many may be chosen.

min_selections.description: Minimum number of options that must be selected (omit for no floor).

max_selections.description: Maximum number of options that may be selected (omit for no ceiling).

text.title: Fill in the blank
text.description: A free-text answer (fill-in-the-blank). The response schema is a string; optional placeholder and multiline hints are props.

rank.title: Rank list
rank.description: Order the options by preference (rank-list). The response schema is an ordered permutation of the option ids; the options live in props. Optional max_ranked limits the answer to the top N (omit to rank them all).

max_ranked.description: Rank only the top N options rather than the full list (omit to rank all).

age-request.title: Encrypted secret request
age-request.description: Request a secret encrypted to an age recipient (replaces the dedicated secret-request path, task_713). The response schema is a string holding the age ciphertext, produced client-side, so no plaintext is ever stored on the board. props.recipient is the age public key to encrypt to.

recipient.description: age public key (recipient) the secret is encrypted to, client-side

string-list.title: List of strings
string-list.description: Enter an arbitrary, dynamically-sized list of strings (add / remove rows), submitted as an array of strings. The response schema is an array of strings. Optional min_items / max_items bound how many rows, placeholder sets the per-row hint, and item_label names a row (e.g. "item" -> "Add item").

min_items.description: Minimum number of non-empty rows required (UI defaults to 1 if omitted).

max_items.description: Maximum number of rows that may be submitted (omit for no ceiling).

item_label.description: Singular noun for a row, e.g. "item" so the add button reads "Add item".

numeric.title: Number
numeric.description: A single bounded number (a count, size, or threshold). The response schema is a number (or integer) with optional minimum / maximum / multipleOf, validated generically; this element renders a numeric input enforcing the same bounds. Optional step, placeholder, and a short unit label are props.

minimum.description: Inclusive lower bound for the entered value (mirror of the response schema's minimum).

maximum.description: Inclusive upper bound for the entered value (mirror of the response schema's maximum).

integer.description: Require a whole number (the response schema uses type integer rather than number).

step.description: Granularity of the input stepper, e.g. 0.5; omit for the browser default of 1 / any.

unit.description: A short unit label shown beside the input, e.g. "ms", "%", "MB".

slider.title: Slider
slider.description: A bounded continuous estimate (a percentage, budget, or any approximate number) rendered as a range slider with a live value readout -- the same number answer as the numeric element, validated against the question's inline response_schema. Both bounds are required so the slider can draw its track; step sets the granularity, integer snaps to whole numbers, and unit is a short label.

minimum.description: Inclusive lower bound (slider track start; mirror of the response schema's minimum).

maximum.description: Inclusive upper bound (slider track end; mirror of the response schema's maximum).

integer.description: Snap to whole numbers (the response schema uses type integer rather than number).

step.description: Slider granularity, e.g. 5; omit for 1 (integer) or continuous (number).

unit.description: A short unit label shown with the value readout, e.g. "%", "ms", "MB".
